clue.text: Stoop, like 'European, in a pronounced way

indicators.note: said in a pronounced way, the word for a European from Denmark is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a Dane is a European, a native of Denmark

explanation.surface: Someone bending down in a markedly Continental manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pronounced way' looks like 'conspicuously' but signals a sound-alike: DANE, a Danish European, is said the same as the word for condescending to act.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend to do something is to lower oneself, and stoop is used in exactly that figurative sense.

clue.text: Deft clue — anagram one inserted is tricky

indicators.note: inserted tells us the letter for one goes into the middle of the rearrangement
the clue simply announces that the two words before it are to be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crossword setter admitting one of his own clues is a cunning anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: a setter boasting of a deft clue. The anagram letters are DECETFUL before 'inserted' adds the I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deceitful sets out to mislead, which is what being tricky means.

clue.text: It holds up a writer how, silly!

indicators.note: holds means the word It wraps round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece reads from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writer, something that writes

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a writer's foolishness for holding things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only works because this is a down clue: the writer, read upwards, sits inside It. 'how' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or foolish, so silly or absurd.

clue.text: Nerve endings confine the antidepressant

indicators.note: the endings are the first and last letters of the word before

parts.note: to pen is to confine or shut in
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug that limits nerve damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nerve endings' sounds like anatomy but gives N and E, the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepenthe is the drug of forgetfulness in the Odyssey that banished grief, so an antidote to sorrow.

clue.text: Magnetic North, as seen on globe ? First-rate

definitions.text: Magnetic North, as seen on globe
definitions.meaning: the magnetic pole sits at the top of a globe and attracts, or draws, compass needles, so it is the thing that draws at the top
of the highest class or quality, from the best drawer of a chest

explanation.surface: A geography lesson about where magnetic north appears on a globe, then a verdict of excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half literally: the magnetic pole sits at the top of the globe and pulls compass needles towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest drawer in a chest held the best things, so the phrase came to mean of the finest social or professional class.

clue.text: Trade unions provide cover for members on boards

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union; the plural gives one
and the plural gives a second TU

explanation.surface: Labour organisations offering protection to company directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members on boards' suggests company directors, but they are a ballerina's limbs, and the boards are the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's short frilled skirt covers the legs, the dancer's members, when on the stage.

clue.text: Chaplain has tea at the end, with part of Bible and sacred music

indicators.note: at the end means the letters for tea are moved from the front of Chaplain to the back

parts.note: taken as written
cha is slang for tea
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes a cup of tea, with scripture and hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has tea at the end' takes CHA from the front of CHAPLAIN and moves it to the end, making PLAINCHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainchant is unaccompanied liturgical singing in the medieval church, so music for worship.

clue.text: Specially armed Crimean soldier

definitions.meaning: having a special kind of sleeve, set in by seams running up to the collar
Lord ... commanded British forces in the Crimean War

explanation.surface: A soldier in the Crimea carrying unusual weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'armed' means sleeved, not carrying weapons. The sleeve was named after the Crimean War commander, Lord Raglan, who lost an arm at Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: The sleeve style that runs to the collar is named after the British commander in the Crimean War.

clue.text: Executors have such self-control

definitions.meaning: executors carry out a will, so they have the authority it gives
determination and restraint

explanation.surface: A remark that executioners are good at restraining themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executors' are the people who carry out a dead person's testament, and the power they hold is that testament's.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength of mind lets one resist temptation, which is self-control.

clue.text: Blame one laid on head of Dean Swift

indicators.note: in a down clue, laid on puts one piece directly above the next

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word after

explanation.surface: Blame placed on the satirist Dean Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dean Swift' looks like Jonathan Swift, Dean of St Patrick's, but Swift alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift both mean very fast.

clue.text: A pectoral disaster for her

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruin, so the letters of the two words before it are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A calamity at someone's breast proves fatal for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges A PECTORAL. The whole clue also tells the story: the Egyptian queen died from an asp's bite at her breast, a disaster of the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Ptolemaic queen of Egypt is said to have killed herself by letting an asp bite her breast.

clue.text: Energetic steps taken to reverse delay in mail

indicators.note: to reverse tells us to turn each of the two following words' equivalents back to front in place

parts.note: lag is a delay or time gap
PO is the Post Office, which handles mail

explanation.surface: Late post being turned round with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns LAG into GAL and PO into OP, giving the lively dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a fast, lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance, so a series of energetic steps.

clue.text: Design, in early construction of St Paul's

parts.note: taken as written
St Paul was a tentmaker by trade, so his early handiwork was a tent

explanation.surface: Plans for the first stage of building the London cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St Paul's' suggests the London cathedral, but it is the apostle, who made tents (Acts 18:3) before his missionary work.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent is purpose or aim, and design can mean a plan or purpose held in mind.

clue.text: Such a player not equipped for the top ?

definitions.text: Such a player not equipped for the top ?

parts.words: Such a player not equipped for the top ?
parts.note: read literally, a player with nothing on his head; in sport, one never awarded a cap for playing for his country

explanation.surface: A sportsman who lacks the kit, or the class, for the highest level.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player selected for the national team is said to win a cap; one never chosen has no cap, which is also nothing on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who has never been picked for the national side has received no international cap, so has nothing for his head.

clue.text: Silly rhymes, whether one likes it or not

definitions.meaning: a nonsense pair of rhyming words, both rhyming with silly

definitions.text: whether one likes it or not
definitions.meaning: regardless of wishes

explanation.surface: A remark that nonsense verse is forced on us anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from 'will I, nill I', meaning whether I want to or not.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless of anyone's wishes, from old 'will he, nill he'.

clue.text: Direct example of 15

parts.note: 15 down is a word meaning a bank, built from two parts; the Forth is an example of the first part, a Scottish river
right is an example of the second part of 15 down, a side

explanation.surface: A straightforward instance of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 down splits into two words: the Forth is a river in Scotland and right is a side, and together they give the word for plain-spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forthright speaks plainly and frankly, which is to be direct.

clue.text: Bank manager's final letter, oddly derisive.

indicators.note: final letter means the last letter of the word manager's
oddly means the letters of the word after are arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: A bank manager's last letter to a customer was strangely scornful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank manager' suggests finance, but the bank is the river's: R ends manager's, and 'oddly' rearranges DERISIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The riverside is the land beside a river, its bank.

clue.text: Vessel — we're bringing stern round

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the last letter of the word before is brought round to the front

explanation.surface: Sailors turning their ship about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing stern round' moves the last letter E of WERE to the front. Vessel and stern point to a ship, but the vessel is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a vessel for holding water.

clue.text: Dog delights shepherd

definitions.meaning: a gundog, the Irish breed with a chestnut coat
the saying 'red sky at night, shepherd's delight': a sun that goes down red pleases the shepherd

explanation.surface: A dog that pleases the shepherd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shepherd' suggests a sheepdog, but this is the weather proverb: a sun setting red at night is the shepherd's delight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish gundog with a glossy chestnut coat; split, the name also means a sun going down red.

clue.text: Surprised to find the first part was first

parts.note: the start is the first part of something
led means was first, was in front

explanation.surface: Someone shocked to learn their opening section came first.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled means given a sudden shock, so surprised.

clue.text: Pointless reason for world revolution

definitions.meaning: in tennis a score of nil is called ..., so having no points
the saying that it is what makes the world go round

explanation.surface: A futile cause for a global uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world revolution' suggests politics, but it is the earth turning: the song says love makes the world go round.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis term for a score of zero, so it means having no points.

clue.text: Like Defoe's Englishman under it all, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Defoe's satire The True-Born Englishman calls him 'that vain ... thing, an Englishman'
unwell by nature: sick at heart, deep down

explanation.surface: A description of a literary character's true disposition.
explanation.walkthrough: Defoe's 1701 poem The True-Born Englishman mocks the English as 'that vain ill-natured thing'. Split, the word also reads as sick by nature, ill under it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone surly and spiteful has a bad temper, which Defoe's poem says of the typical English person.

clue.text: No pot-shot with this, gun

definitions.meaning: in billiards, a shot in which the cue ball strikes two balls in turn, without potting either
a large artillery piece

explanation.surface: A gun not suited to taking casual shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot-shot' looks like a careless gunshot, but in billiards a shot hitting two balls in succession pots nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a heavy artillery gun and a billiards shot striking two balls one after the other.

clue.text: Put a brave face on it? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Put a brave face on it? Just the opposite

parts.words: Put a brave face on it? Just the opposite
parts.note: turn the phrase round: not put a brave face on it but put it on a brave's face, a brave being a warrior

explanation.surface: Advice to bear up cheerfully, promptly contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: A brave is a Native American warrior; what such a warrior puts on his face before battle is decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured decoration was applied to a warrior's face and body before battle.

clue.text: Grown like this, it's an offence

indicators.note: like this tells us the word Grown is rearranged into the form the answer shows

explanation.surface: A complaint that something that has grown this way is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this' signals that GROWN rearranged gives the answer, an anagram announced by pointing at itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong is an injustice or offence done to someone.

clue.text: The last production from Paddy, we hear

definitions.meaning: a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped form, and a heavy shoe is made on one
the Irish accent one hears from an Irishman, Paddy being slang for one

explanation.surface: The final show put on by an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' is the cobbler's form, not 'final'; 'Paddy' is a nickname for an Irishman, whose lilting accent has the same name as a stout leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sturdy ornamented leather shoe and a strong Irish accent.

clue.text: Gather information alternately with the French

annotationWithheld.why: Gather information alternately with the French (5): GEN (information) interleaved letter by letter with LA (the French) gives G-L-E-A-N; the grammar has no interleave operation to express it
annotationWithheld.clue: Gather information alternately with the French

clue.text: Keen, in a tizzy once ?. .

parts.note: a tizzy was old slang for a sixpence, written VI D, six pence

explanation.surface: Someone enthusiastic but flustered in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks old money: a tizzy was a pre-decimal British sixpence, written VI D. The surface suggests 'in a tizzy', flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, which is what keen means.

clue.text: Head gardener's produce

definitions.meaning: slang for the head
a bulb vegetable grown in vegetable plots

explanation.surface: A head gardener's crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head gardener' reads as one job title, but Head is a definition on its own: the British slang 'off your onion' means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulb vegetable is grown in kitchen gardens and is also British slang for the head.

clue.text: Even better? Even better

parts.note: level means even or flat
to best someone is to better or outdo them

explanation.surface: A question about improvement, answered by repeating it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Even better?' is a playful definition, the most even of all; the second takes each word in turn, even as LEVEL and better as the verb BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's utmost is giving every effort, playfully read here as being as even as possible.

clue.text: This monster caused the death of Desdemona.

definitions.text: This monster caused the death of Desdemona.

parts.words: This monster caused the death of Desdemona.
parts.note: in Othello jealousy is called the monster with a particular colour of eyes, and Othello's jealousy drives him to kill his wife

explanation.surface: A creature responsible for killing the heroine of Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago warns Othello against jealousy, 'the green-eyed monster', which leads him to smother Desdemona.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealous or envious, from Iago's description of jealousy as a monster with eyes of that colour.

clue.text: Paid in some countries for ordinary, share?

indicators.note: a share is a portion of something, so the answer is a portion of the letters of the word after it

explanation.surface: A question about what an ordinary share pays abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordinary share' is a stock-market term, but 'share' takes part of ORDINARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency of several countries, such as Kuwait and Serbia, so money paid there.
